mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing discount rates for equity valuations and generating positive forward returns in the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Federal funds rate was 2.63% in March 2005, down from 4.75% in 2001, indicating a prolonged easing cycle
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in periods where FEDFUNDS declines > 0.5pp over 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll growth above 150k per month signals strong labor market demand, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 150k in the prior month
evidence_refs: fact:PAYEMS rose from 132,926k to 133,154k between February and March 2005, indicating labor market strength
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when PAYEMS growth exceeds 150k, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in residential investment (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) signals strong aggregate demand, leading to higher corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:HOUST rose from 2,195k to 2,207k between February and March 2005, while RSAFS declined from 339,299M to 326,179M
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when both HOUST and RSAFS rise simultaneously, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (2017=100) indicates a contraction in real output, signaling economic weakness and potential recession, which triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:INDPRO fell from 118.527 to 96.4456 between February and March 2005, indicating a significant contraction
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when INDPRO < 100, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% year-over-year, combined with a stable or rising federal funds rate, signals persistent inflationary pressure, prompting the Fed to maintain tight policy, which suppresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:CPIAUCSL rose from 192.0 to 192.4 between February and March 2005, indicating inflationary momentum
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY and FEDFUNDS >= 2.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption (RSAFS) above 330 billion dollars, combined with rising housing starts (HOUST), indicates strong consumer and housing demand, which drives corporate revenue growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:RSAFS was 326,179M in March 2005, near 330B threshold; HOUST was 2,207k, above 2,200k
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when both RSAFS > 330B and HOUST > 2,200k, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.0% and a rise in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 150k indicates a tightening labor market, increasing wage pressures and inflation expectations, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated rate hikes.
evidence_refs: fact:UNRATE was 5.2% in March 2005, just above 5.0%; PAYEMS rose from 132,926k to 133,154k
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when UNRATE < 5.0% and PAYEMS growth > 150k, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) above 3% annualized growth, combined with rising residential investment (HOUST), signals strong economic momentum, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:GDPC1 was revised to 15,670.88B in October 2004, indicating strong growth; HOUST was 2,207k in March 2005
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when both GDPC1 and HOUST are rising, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
